body:
CURRENT MERGER PROCEDURE. Scope: the currently authorized Coder/Merger workflow. This memory records operating guidance; recover the acting project's current STOP/resume and authority before execution.

1. The Merger is non-authoring. The Coder implements, runs focused/new tests, freezes and obtains the independent reviews. Select focused tests for dependency impact, including existing architecture/boundary guards when calls cross components. Excluded affected guards remain unverified; no Coder full gate is added. The package names scope, base, patch/root, fingerprint, test outcomes, full reviews and finding dispositions.
2. READY requires complete independent reviews covering the package's code, tests and docs, with full results, coverage and finding dispositions; an unread in-scope gap is not clean. Each host-issued review attempt, including a same-delegation follow-up, needs its own structured result before the final reply. 'Exactly once' means per attempt, not session lifetime. Missing/failed submission is unavailable; prose cannot replace it. The existing parent owns supported recovery; no duplicate pair.
At startup/compaction/replacement, Engram reviewer leaves follow AGENTS.md Start and resume before inspection: list all memory keys through continuations, then read relevant CURRENT full bodies. Do not repeat completed recovery in the same context. The Coder includes these recovery instructions and applicable current rules in the initial brief; receiving a brief does not waive the required reads. The leaf reports recovery/access gaps and the current keys/revisions read. Close a missing-read gap once with the same reviewer on the unchanged freeze before treating its review as complete; do not repeat tests, launch another pair or require unrelated memories. Do not append routine supplements after that gap is closed.
Reviews finish before complete READY. The Merger may carry the unchanged reviewed contribution onto current master without a new pair solely for base movement, including executable, build or governing changes. Record freeze evidence and exact-blob equality or a three-way identical-hunk proof for regular text, plus the Merger's dependency/conflict assessment. Do not claim the prior review covered new master content. Several complete packages may share a clean final tree without another Merger pair. Actual conflicts, changed package content or unproven unchanged contribution return to the Coder for an appropriately reviewed package. Review evidence alone does not invalidate a check on identical final input; content corrections need applicable new validation. No landing, rebase, force-push or policy waiver is implied.
3. CODER TO MERGER: send one complete READY with recipient-readable durable exports of every full authoritative review packet and complete reviewer output, their hashes and reviewed freeze. Parent-scoped delegation ids or 'I read it' alone do not transfer evidence. Keep test/review progress on the task/coordinator. Route new material defects or collaboration failures to their proper owner.
4. Integrate onto current main/master. Return conflicts and required corrections to the Coder, who returns a tested and appropriately reviewed new input. Check ancestry and content to avoid duplicating an already-landed change.
5. Prepare dependencies and disk in the integration root, freeze the final tree and run one standard full gate on that tree. Only a complete PASS bound to the identical final input is reusable. A different tree needs its applicable gate. Missing tools and unrun stages are not passes. Use actual terminal stage outcomes and matching fingerprints as evidence. Check each native command's expected exit status and complete evidence artifact before dependent actions or success reports; unexpected failure blocks those steps until diagnosed. Record raw, filtered and index hashes and EOL separately; normalized equality is not raw-byte equality.
6. Under Greg's current workflow, host credit, acceptance evaluations and an additional Merger-side review are not extra merge conditions. Proceed through the acting session's authorized landing path once the applicable reviews and tests pass. Preserve exact-build and Git safety requirements; do not infer rebase, force-push or restart authority.
7. Acceptance evaluations are deferred. Keep technically landed items open as "DOSTARCZONO — EWALUACJA PENDING" with landing evidence until later direct instruction. Do not schedule closure evaluations, change acceptance policy or bypass native done. Missing evaluation does not block unrelated authorized merge work. See rules-greg-checkin-tests-review-stop-evaluations-2026-10-24 for this current decision.
8. Use supported claims, recovery and handoffs. A foreign live claim is not bypassed by impersonation, store edits or clock changes. Claims grant no filesystem/Git authority. Handoff of a separately held task may proceed during another task's gate when it leaves that gate's claim, root, source and input unchanged; keep attribution and actual resource limits intact.
9. Use durable result wakes in the run's own project where available. Record the run, owner, next action and recovery route. A wake failure prompts recovery of the existing result, not a test rerun. Queue state belongs on tasks.
10. Apply rules-post-completion-cleanup: record REMOVE/RETAIN decisions and concrete owners/end conditions. Preserve roots/evidence still needed by open tasks or active runs. Cleanup is a post-completion responsibility, not an added landing gate.

Before handing a merge queue to a new session, resolve its exact live root id and verify its actual project/workdir and tracker/tool binding match that queue. A display name is not proof of project binding. If the session was deleted/recreated, rediscover its replacement and address native offers to the new live session; do not reuse the old identity or treat old delivery as receipt by its replacement.

Each canonical procedure has one named editor and a named successor. Merger2 edits TermAl merger-operating-procedure; Fable2/Coders send corrections to him. Consolidate and full-read verify the current body. Across projects send exact correction plus source revision; recipients verify their own current procedure and distinguish source reads from quoted-text reads. Project-scoped memory_not_found is an access gap. Before publishing, read available pages in that rule's thread and reconcile withdrawals/supersession. Correct later withdrawals promptly and record any use of old wording. Record actual delivery/publication times; queued but unread mail is not known. This adds no approval wait.

MERGER TO ARCHITECT3: report only concrete collaboration failures that need a workflow/rule correction. Describe the failed interaction, evidence, impact and current owner. Routine START/PASS/FAIL test status, READY/accepted-package status, queue/landing/install updates and routine repair progress go to the task and operational coordinator, not Architect3. A product test failure goes to Architect3 only when it exposes a collaboration failure needing his intervention. Do not register Architect3 as a routine test --notify recipient, result relay or recovery owner; the coordinator and Merger own those routes. Existing runs continue through their operational owners.

Architect3 diagnoses collaboration failures, corrects the current rule and informs affected agents. Check effects from task evidence; no routine compliance mail. Report failures to Architect3 and the project coordinator. Only project coordinators relay project information through Advisor; Advisor never executes work. Keep incident histories and discarded assumptions in task notes; current bodies contain current rules.
